For CONTACT and PROPERTY that vocabulary is enumerable: listFilterFieldNames returns it complete, and a field it lists is a field a conditional can evaluate. NEVER tell a user an automation cannot consider some attribute without reading that list for the workflow DOMAIN first — property attributes (last sold date, year built, estimated value) are evaluable in a PROPERTY workflow and are not contact fields, so "the automation cannot see it" is usually a domain mismatch rather than a missing capability. DEAL and APPOINTMENT conditionals take their own full filter group the same way, but listFilterFieldNames and listFilterFields accept CONTACT and PROPERTY only. That is a gap in DISCOVERY, never evidence about the capability: read the existing graph with getWorkflowVersionGraph and copy the shape of a conditional already in it, and if you cannot establish that a field is evaluable there, say you could not confirm it rather than reporting that it cannot be done. AI CONDITION CONTEXT — an "ai_conditional" step's `context` is a Context Layer SELECTION, not a list of ids: an object whose keys are any of contact | deal | property | appointment | organization, each mapping to that source's slice flags (e.g. {contact:{includeTextMessages:true, includeNotes:false}}). A key's PRESENCE is the include decision; an absent key is not sent at all, and an empty object {} means that source with its provider defaults. Only the sources the RUN carries an id for resolve — a CONTACT run has a contact, a PROPERTY run a property — so a selection naming a source the domain's runs never carry renders nothing. The step is available on APPOINTMENT graphs even though "conditional" is not, and unavailable on EVENT, where a webhook payload has no context object to render. EVENT MAPPINGS — the two rules an event step's mapping rows are REJECTED for, which no field name states. (1) EXACTLY ONE destination and EXACTLY ONE value source per row: a customFieldMappings row names either a customFieldId or an attributionKey (one of the org's reserved, listing-hidden attribution fields: utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term, utm_content, gclid, fbclid, msclkid, ttclid, li_fat_id, landingUrl, referrerUrl), and either an accessor or a literalValue. A row naming two of either is dropped and counted at execution, never resolved by precedence, because guessing which half you meant would silently write a field you did not name. (2) A tagMappings row resolves its value to a tag or list BY NAME and CREATES one when the org has none, bounded at 25 distinct values per row and refusing values that are obviously not category names (a uuid, an email, a url, a long-digit platform id, over 80 characters); tag and list names share one org-wide namespace, so a name a list already holds cannot also become a tag and that row is dropped. Both counts ride the run's FIND_CREATE_CONTACT_RESOLVED audit event as tagsWritten/tagsDropped. MERGE FIELDS — the COMPLETE per-domain vocabulary a body may draw on. Substituted at run time: textBody, textBodies, emailBody, emailSubject, a Slack block's text and a Slack button's url, plus a deal node's title and a task node's name and description. NOT substituted, so braces there are left alone: a generative node's systemPrompt (an instruction to a model, not a template) and a deal node's description. Keys are matched EXACTLY and are case-sensitive. There is NO dotted record namespace: {{contact.address1}}, {{contact.firstName}} and {{deal.title}} are not merge fields (the SLACK keys below are the only dotted ones, and they are literal names, not a namespace you may extend). Do not infer a key from another domain's spelling either — the shapes genuinely differ (CONTACT has contactPropertyAddress, PROPERTY has full_address), so use a key off this list or none. An unknown token is NOT a missing variable and does NOT render blank: braces reach the reader verbatim (except a notify step on OMIT_BLANKS, which blanks them). promoteWorkflowDraft REFUSES a draft carrying one in a SCANNED FIELD — textBody, textBodies, emailBody (including one stored as emailBodyFormat "TIPTAP_JSON", whose merge fields are document pills rather than braces and are read as such), a NODE'S OWN emailSubject, a Slack block's text or its button url, a deal node's title and fallbackDealTitle on a CONTACT or DEAL graph, and an inline task node's name and description — and updateWorkflowGraph returns that same judgement as workflowGroup.draftValidation on every write — a reading of the GROUP'S DRAFT, which is the version you just wrote whenever you followed the normal path and edited the draft. Edit a PAUSED version instead and the field still answers about the draft, so it is null when there is none and about a DIFFERENT version when there is: it is not a verdict on your write in that case, and nothing in the response says so ({isValid, errors}, each unrenderable token named with the field it sits in and the supported key it most likely meant). READ IT on the response to the write and fix what it names, rather than discovering it when activation fails. THAT LIST OF SCANNED FIELDS IS CLOSED, and it is still SHORTER than the list of fields that are substituted. Anything substituted at run time but absent from it is checked by nothing, so a clean draftValidation is not evidence about it — check those against the vocabulary below yourself. What remains unscanned, and NOT an exhaustive list: the WORKFLOW-LEVEL email subject on communicationConfig — which is the subject that actually ships whenever sendInSameThread is not false, i.e. by default, and the scan only ever walks NODES; every FALLBACK field (fallbackTextBody, fallbackEmailSubject, fallbackEmailBody), each substituted by its executor under SEND_FALLBACK; a PROPERTY create-contact step's deal title and fallback title (substituted against the NEW CONTACT and the workflow user, not against the PROPERTY graph's own vocabulary, so the gate has no single vocabulary to judge them by and deliberately does not try); a Slack reply node's message; and any body that lives in a referenced templateId rather than in the graph — the graph then carries no body for the scan to look at. In every one of them a wrong key promotes clean. What the recipient then sees differs by path and the difference matters: most render through the token renderer and arrive as LITERAL BRACES, but a Slack reply node's message is interpolated by its own function, which replaces any {{slack.<field>}} it does not recognise with an EMPTY STRING — so a typo there is not visible as a broken template at all, it is simply missing text. PROPERTY: {{line1}}, {{line2}}, {{propertyCity}}, {{state}}, {{zip}}, {{full_address}}, {{property_url}}, {{beds}}, {{baths}}, {{sqft}}. CONTACT: {{fullName}}, {{firstName}}, {{lastName}}, {{contactUrl}}, {{contactPhoneNumber}}, {{contactEmail}}, {{contactPropertyAddress}}, {{contactPropertyFullAddress}}, {{contactPropertyCity}}, {{contactPropertyZipcode}}, {{userFullName}}, {{userFirstName}}, {{userLastName}}, {{userPhoneNumber}}, {{userEmail}}, {{userOrganizationName}}. DEAL: {{dealTitle}}, {{dealUrl}}, {{dealPipelineName}}, {{dealStageName}}, {{dealPropertyLine1}}, {{dealPropertyLine2}}, {{dealPropertyCity}}, {{dealPropertyState}}, {{dealPropertyZip}}, {{dealPropertyFullAddress}}, {{dealContactFullName}}, {{dealContactFirstName}}, {{dealContactLastName}}. APPOINTMENT: {{appointmentStartTime}}, {{appointmentEndTime}}, {{appointmentMeetingLink}}, {{appointmentLocation}}, {{appointmentDurationMinutes}}, {{fullName}}, {{firstName}}, {{lastName}}, {{contactUrl}}, {{contactPhoneNumber}}, {{contactEmail}}, {{contactPropertyAddress}}, {{contactPropertyFullAddress}}, {{contactPropertyCity}}, {{contactPropertyZipcode}}, {{userFullName}}, {{userFirstName}}, {{userLastName}}, {{userPhoneNumber}}, {{userEmail}}, {{userOrganizationName}}. EVENT: no merge fields at all — a {{...}} in an EVENT body is an ACCESSOR PATH into the inbound webhook payload (see the EVENT actions above), not a merge field, and is never validated against this vocabulary. SLACK: {{slack.text}}, {{slack.userName}}, {{slack.channelName}}, {{slack.permalink}}.  Two conditional keys, and neither is legal on every graph: {{agentName}} resolves ONLY where the graph's TEXT sender is a marketing campaign, and a contact CUSTOM FIELD — addressable as {{ContactTag_<uuid>}}, where the uuid is a CUSTOM-FIELD id from listContactCustomFields and NOT a tag id from searchContactTags, however much the prefix suggests otherwise (ContactTag is the table that stores tags, lists and custom fields alike, so the GRN is named for the table rather than for the thing; a real tag id passes the shape check, is accepted by promote, and renders empty) — resolves ONLY on CONTACT and APPOINTMENT graphs, the ones a send loads contact context for — and on an APPOINTMENT graph only from the TEXT REMINDER, which renders with the task, the contact and the user. An appointment Slack post loads the task alone, so every CONTACT key there, tags included, renders literally even though promote accepts it: the gate judges per DOMAIN, and this is the one place a domain is wider than one of its own nodes. Used outside its condition either one is unrenderable and blocks promote exactly like an unknown key.Triggers are managed through the `triggers` array: each entry is upserted by its id (mint a fresh UUID to add one) and entries omitted from the array are detached; only `config` syncs (`name` is cosmetic). Trigger config shapes: {type: "manual"}, {type: "created"}, {type: "mutation", filter: <FilterGroup>}, {type: "match", filter: <FilterGroup>}; CONTACT-only: {type: "inbound_text", twilioPhoneNumberIds: [...]}, {type: "inbound_email", connectedAccountIds?: [...]}; EVENT workflows have exactly one trigger shape, {type: "event_received"} — the workflow's minted webhook URL is the trigger. Minimal valid drip example (node/edge shape): nodes: [{id:"n1",type:"trigger",config:{}}, {id:"n2",type:"text_action",config:{mode:"single",textBody:"Hi {{firstName}}"}}, {id:"n3",type:"wait",config:{mode:"fixed",seconds:172800,interruptEnabled:false,interruptFilter:{id:"f1",operator:"AND",conditions:[],groups:[]}}}, {id:"n4",type:"end",config:{}}], edges: [{id:"e1",config:{},parentNodeId:"n1",childNodeId:"n2"}, {id:"e2",config:{},parentNodeId:"n2",childNodeId:"n3"}, {id:"e3",config:{},parentNodeId:"n3",childNodeId:"n4"}]. PROMOTE GOTCHA: a template-less TEXT/EMAIL draft starts with communicationConfig.<channel>.sender {type: "UNSET"}, and promoteWorkflowDraft rejects SenderNotChosen — set a real sender in the automation config (e.g. {type: "POINT_PERSON"}) before promoting; getWorkflow.draftValidation names this and any other blocking issues. GRAPH CONFIG — `graph.config`, the settings an operator asks for by name. It sits beside `nodes`/`edges`/`triggers` and is NOT per-node. Shared keys (every domain): `triggerOperator` "AND"|"OR" (whether a graph with several triggers needs all of them or any one); `activation.triggerEligibleRecordsNow` (on activation, enroll records that ALREADY match, not just future ones); and `triggerWindow`, which limits when ENROLLMENT may happen; `exclusiveEnrollment` true means a record entering THIS workflow is unenrolled from every OTHER workflow it is still running under — those runs are STOPPED at the moment this one is created (other WORKFLOW, so a prior version of this same workflow is left alone), which is how "only one campaign at a time per lead" is expressed. It is inert on EVENT graphs, whose runs anchor on a webhook payload rather than a record. CONTACT graphs add `exitConditions.exitConditionTypes` — any of "any_inbound_communication", "inbound_text", "inbound_email", "contact_archived", "outbound_from_human", "outbound_from_ai_employee", "outbound_from_other_workflow" — which is how "stop the drip as soon as they reply" is expressed; there is no per-node way to say it. The "outbound_from_*" three end the run when somebody ELSE messages the contact while it is live; a run never ends on a message its own workflow group sent. APPOINTMENT graphs accept the `exitConditions` key but it carries nothing (typed `undefined`), so exit conditions are effectively CONTACT-only. `communicationConfig` is NOT contact-only: CONTACT and APPOINTMENT graphs both take it, and it is where an appointment reminder's quiet hours and sender live too. SEND WINDOW — `sendWindow` (on communicationConfig) and `triggerWindow` (top level) are ALMOST the same shape: {timezone, daysOfWeek?:["MON".."SUN"], startTime?:{hour,minute}, endTime?:{hour,minute}, timezoneMode?}. They differ in exactly one field. `sendWindow.timezoneMode` accepts "BUSINESS"|"RECIPIENT"|"CONFIGURED"; `triggerWindow.timezoneMode` accepts only "RECIPIENT"|"CONFIGURED", and passing "BUSINESS" there is REJECTED by the graph parser — enrollment is evaluated with no organisation clock to read it on, so the schema does not offer a mode its evaluator cannot honour. `hour` AND `minute` are BOTH REQUIRED on each time — {hour:9} alone is rejected by the graph parser. These are clock times, not offsets, so "weekdays 9-6 Central" is daysOfWeek MON..FRI with startTime {hour:9,minute:0} and endTime {hour:18,minute:0}. A channel that configures NOTHING is not unrestricted: it falls back to 08:00-21:00 Eastern, the TCPA envelope. Say that rather than implying a missing window means any hour. `timezoneMode` says WHOSE clock those times are read on, and it changes when a message actually goes out. "BUSINESS" reads them in the ORGANISATION's own timezone, read live at evaluation (New York when the organisation never set one) — 9:00 means 9:00 at the operator's desk, one instant per day for everybody, and the schedule moves if the organisation does. "RECIPIENT" reads them in each recipient's own zone, derived from their phone number's area code — 9:00 means 9:00 where the lead is, so one schedule fires at a different instant per contact; a number whose zone cannot be derived (toll-free, non-NANP) and EMAIL, which has no area code at all, read the organisation's clock instead. "CONFIGURED" reads them in the window's own `timezone` for everybody, fixed, whatever the organisation does — the mode that follows nobody. NO mode adds a quiet-hours FLOOR on a workflow send window — the window as written is the window that runs, so a 01:00-05:00 "RECIPIENT" window delivers at 01:00 in each lead's own zone. The 08:00-21:00 TCPA envelope is the DEFAULT for a channel that configures nothing, not a clamp on one that does. AN OMITTED `sendWindow.timezoneMode` IS NOT A CONSTANT: it reads as the organisation's business clock once that organisation is on it and as the recipient's before that, so state the mode explicitly whenever the answer matters. A `triggerWindow` gates ENROLLMENT and has no recipient and no send, so its `timezoneMode` is inert either way — those times are always read in the window's own `timezone`. SENDER — `communicationConfig.text.sender` / `.email.sender`, both allowed at once. A mode name alone is not a valid sender: most modes carry required fields. TEXT: {type:"UNSET"} | {type:"POINT_PERSON"} | {type:"MEETING_OWNER"} (appointment graphs) | {type:"PHONE", fromPhoneNumberId} | {type:"RANDOM_PHONE", fromPhoneNumberIds:[...]} | {type:"LOCAL_PRESENCE", scope, fallback} — LOCAL_PRESENCE picks a team number whose area code matches the recipient, and BOTH scope and fallback are required: scope is {kind:"ALL_TEAM"} | {kind:"SPECIFIC", fromPhoneNumberIds} | {kind:"EXCLUDE", excludedPhoneNumberIds} | {kind:"MARKETING_CAMPAIGN", ...}, and a MARKETING_CAMPAIGN scope accepts ONLY the {type:"SCOPE_POOL"} fallback. EMAIL: {type:"UNSET"} | {type:"POINT_PERSON"} | {type:"IDENTITY", fromEmail, fromClientId} | {type:"RANDOM_IDENTITY", identities:[...]}. UNSET is the creation default and activation is GATED on replacing it, so a graph left on UNSET will not run. SYSTEM CATEGORY — the separate `systemCategory` variable, not part of the graph. CONTACT, DEAL, EVENT and APPOINTMENT all allow CUSTOM workflows, so `null` is correct there — do NOT attach a category to make an appointment reminder. PROPERTY is the one domain that allows no custom workflow at all: it MUST carry "PROPERTY_SIGNAL_SKIP_TRACE", and creating one without a category is rejected with "Custom workflows are not available for property — pick a template." A non-null `systemCategory` ALSO requires a `templateId` on the same create — "A system-category workflow needs a template id" — so a category alone still fails. Both rejections read as "property workflows are not supported" if you do not know the pair is required. NO domain offers "APPOINTMENT_REMINDER" or "INTEGRATION_LEAD_HANDLING" at create time: both are READ-only on an existing workflow, so never pass either here — those domains take custom workflows. The second is minted on integration connect, then LOCKED against adding, deleting or rewiring a step.
